title: 2023 budget: 4.84% tax increase recommended
subtitle: Committee allocated strategic investment funds to traffic calming, parks, trails, recreation and arts, and added garbage collection staff.
overview: On final budget day, the Finance and Corporate Services Committee recommended a 2023 general levy of $146,507,227, about a 4.84% tax increase before tax policy changes, including 1.89% assessment growth. Staff described the increase as below inflation and about $56 a year for a typical taxpayer. The committee also recommended the 2023-2032 capital budget and the enterprise budgets for building, golf, parking, gas, water, sanitary and stormwater.

Most of the day went to deciding how to spend about $1.5 million in strategic investment funding. The committee recommended money for traffic calming, neighbourhood parks, trail paving and free recreation and leisure access. Housing for All studies and arts and culture events were funded from reserves. It also recommended added staffing for Grand River Park and enhanced garbage collection in parks and trails.

These are recommendations. Council must adopt or change them at a special meeting held the same day. A proposal to fund greening of the city's fleet was not funded and is expected to return through the corporate climate action plan.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended a general levy of $146,507,227, about a 4.84% tax increase excluding tax policy changes, including 1.89% assessment growth.
The committee recommended approving the 2023-2032 Capital Budget and Forecast, with expenditures for all years totalling $1,613,535,000.

decisions.item: Free recreational programming and leisure access
decisions.detail: The committee recommended $285,000 from strategic investment funding for options 1, 3, 4 and 5, reduced from the $400,000 first proposed {{vote:m6}}.
The committee recommended $600,000 of strategic investment funding for annual trail paving.
The committee recommended $200,000 from strategic investment funding for traffic calming, after rejecting an amendment to reduce it to $160,000.
The committee recommended $400,000 from strategic investment funding for neighbourhood park improvements.

decisions.item: Enhanced garbage collection in parks and trails
decisions.detail: The committee recommended $50,000 in operating funding for two added full-time staff phased in late in 2023, and directed staff to find existing capital funds for a new compactor truck.
The committee recommended $15,000 of ongoing funding plus a one-time $100,000 from the Economic Development Reserve Fund, primarily for events.

debate: Some councillors urged returning the $1.5 million to the tax base, or spending less of it, citing high food prices, a possible recession and expected regional tax increases. Others said the funded items were low-cost or free services for families and that the money amounted to about a dollar or a few dollars a month per household.

On traffic calming, staff said the $100,000 base option was workable with existing staff, and that going beyond $200,000 would need more traffic staff. One councillor sought $160,000, citing the issue paper's caution about adding more seasonal measures. Supporters said suburban and rural wards have strong demand and the flexibility was worth having.

On recreation, councillors differed over how much to spend and on which options. Some prioritised leisure access card increases and youth programming, while others wanted older-adult programs in neighbourhood centres. Some worried that spending would use up the available funds. Staff said the leisure access program never turns people away when money runs out.

On parks, one councillor argued funding should wait for the Places and Spaces strategy. Others said playgrounds are outdated and that the funding would still fit within that work. On trails, supporters cited year-round routes to schools and transit and equity across wards.

On garbage collection, councillors said overflowing bins and litter had increased, which staff linked to regional collection changes, removal of bus stop bins, heavier trail use and melting snow. One councillor opposed it, saying the region should respond first. Staff said it needs permanent full-time staff and a second compactor truck.
